_note: Despia MCP, both directions (local-ai-engine.md §4.8). THE LAW ENCODED HERE: (1) CLIENT — tools discovered from a remote server join the ONE tool registry NAMESPACED by server (`mcp.<server>.<tool>`), so two servers offering `search` never collide, and they carry their JSON Schema through verbatim. (2) A server the app never declared is not reachable, and a declared server that is down degrades to typed absence with its own tools missing — the rest of the registry keeps working. (3) SERVER — what the app serves is DECLARED, not coded: `facets.mcp` rows map manifest actions and Base queries into MCP tools, the same derivation as module tools, one grammar and two protocols. (4) The local server is LOOPBACK-ONLY with a per-session token, and the token is the boundary, not the interface: a request without it is refused, and the token never appears in a URL (on-device loopback is reachable by co-resident apps). (5) External hosts pair through a 0600 discovery file carrying the current port and a pairing token DISTINCT from in-app session tokens, written only while consent stands and removed when it is withdrawn. (6) A mutating served tool inherits the same approve-before-execute flow and the same Base snapshot as any other mutating tool — the protocol changes nothing about the safety story.

cases.name: mcp: discovered tools join the registry namespaced by server
cases._note: Two servers both offer `search`; both are usable because the namespace is the server id, and the model sees two distinct tools with their own schemas.

cases.name: mcp: a client tool round-trips through the loop
mcp: an undeclared server is not reachable
cases._note: The app's manifest and config are the allowlist. Connecting to a server nobody declared is refused typed — a model cannot talk the app into a new network peer.

cases.name: mcp: a server that is down removes only its own tools
cases._note: Degradation is per-server. The unreachable server's tools vanish from the registry with a typed reason; the working server's tools are untouched and the completion still runs.

cases.name: mcp: served tools are derived from declared rows, not written by hand
cases._note: The local server's tool list comes from `facets.mcp` rows exactly the way the loop's module tools come from `facets.tools` — one derivation, two protocols. A row naming an action gets that action's declared args as its schema.

cases.name: mcp: the local server refuses a request without its session token
cases._note: The boundary, asserted. Loopback is reachable by every co-resident app on the device, so an unauthenticated request is refused — and a wrong token is refused the same way, with no hint about which part was wrong.

cases.name: mcp: an external host pairs through the discovery file only while consent stands
cases._note: Static host configs versus our dynamic port: the discovery file carries the current port and a pairing token that is NOT the in-app session token, it is written 0600, and withdrawing consent removes it. An external host that cached the old token is refused after withdrawal.

cases.name: mcp: a mutating served tool takes the same approval and snapshot path
cases._note: The protocol is not a bypass. A write requested over MCP waits for approval before it executes and runs inside a snapshot, exactly like a write requested by the in-app loop — the fixture is here so the local server can never become the soft path into the user's data.
